privacy_p_collected: The text you enter on the "Start Learning" page and in the AI chat is processed directly in your browser for analysis, and is not sent to or stored on an InvestED server. When you research an asset, only the asset symbol (e.g. NVDA) is sent to InvestED's serverless function to fetch market data.
privacy_p_ai: If you run a local AI model (Ollama) on your computer, the text you write is sent only to the local server running on your computer (localhost) — not to any external cloud service.
privacy_p_cookies: The app stores in your browser's localStorage only: theme preference (light/dark), language preference, learning and quiz progress, analysis history (only with your consent), and local memory records such as watchlists and saved research. All of this stays on your device and can be exported or deleted from the "Data Controls" page. No tracking or advertising cookies are used.
terms_p_1: InvestED is an educational platform for learning about investing. The service does not constitute investment advice, financial advice, tax advice, or a recommendation to take any action in securities.
terms_p_2: All content in the system — including risk scores, investor classifications, sample portfolios, and market data — is presented for educational and illustrative purposes only, and does not constitute a recommendation to take any action. Consult a licensed professional before making investment decisions.
terms_p_3: The system is provided for personal and educational use. Content may not be copied, reproduced, or distributed without attribution.
faq_a_1: No. InvestED is an educational platform only. It does not provide investment recommendations and does not tell users what to invest in. All content — including the broker comparison table — is intended to teach concepts and help with orientation, not to recommend.
faq_q_2: How does the system analyze my profile?
faq_a_2: The system identifies keywords and phrases in the text you wrote (age, goals, risk, time horizon, financial knowledge, interests) and calculates a risk score and investor classification using transparent rules. The Explainable AI card shows exactly which signals were identified.
faq_a_3: Analysis runs in your browser and is not sent to an InvestED server. Some items - such as language preference, learning progress, and analysis history (only with your consent) - are stored locally in your device's localStorage, and can be exported or deleted from the "Data Controls" page. There is no cloud account and no remote sync.
faq_q_4: Are the market data on the dashboard real?
faq_a_4: Yes — in the live production version, market data is fetched in real time from Yahoo Finance, through a dedicated server function. The symbols shown are selected based on the interests identified in your profile. If the service is unavailable (e.g., in local development), the system automatically falls back to simulated data so the dashboard always works.
faq_q_5: How does the personal learning track work?
faq_a_5: The track is tailored to the financial knowledge level you indicated. Beginners get a full track from the basics. Those who already understand the material get a shorter track that starts from the advanced stages, with the basics shown as optional refreshers.

about_general_desc: InvestED is a platform designed to teach investing in an interactive, transparent, and accessible way.
about_p1: InvestED is an independent FinTech product created, designed, and developed entirely by Saar Kessel — MBA and BA in Business Administration, with practical experience in the banking industry from two years at Bank Hapoalim, alongside a deep and ongoing interest in the world of investing, technology, and FinTech.
about_p2: This project is, to a large extent, my business card: it was born out of a clear perception that the investing world is full of terms and concepts that deter many people even to start learning about it, and out of a genuine desire to prove — not just tell — how to combine real financial knowledge with Full Stack development capabilities and advanced AI technologies, in order to turn a complex field into a simple, visual and interactive experience.
about_p3: Beyond the technical aspect, the project reflects an end-to-end Product Thinking approach: from defining the problem (accessibility of financial knowledge), through understanding the user and their needs, to selecting the technological architecture that supports it in the best way possible — exactly as expected from a real production product in a FinTech company.
quiz_q1_o1: A loan given to the government
quiz_q1_o2: A fund that holds a basket of assets and trades like a single stock
quiz_q1_o3: A type of bank savings account
quiz_q1_e: An ETF holds a basket of assets (stocks, bonds, etc.) and trades on the exchange like a stock — it's the simplest way to get immediate diversification.
quiz_q2: What is the main purpose of diversification?
quiz_q2_o2: To reduce risk by spreading across different assets
quiz_q2_e: Diversification is not meant to maximize profit, but to reduce risk — so that poor performance of a single asset won't sink the entire portfolio.
quiz_q3: What usually happens when someone tries to "time the market"?
quiz_q3_o1: It usually works only for professionals
quiz_q3_o2: It's very difficult to consistently predict peaks and troughs, even for experts
quiz_q3_o3: It's the safest way to invest
quiz_q3_e: Many studies show that even professional investors have great difficulty timing the market consistently — time in the market usually beats timing the market.
quiz_q4_o2: Earning returns on returns that have already been earned in the past
quiz_q4_o3: A fee charged by the bank on investments
quiz_q4_e: Compound interest is the engine behind long-term wealth building — money that earns returns, which themselves earn additional returns over time.
quiz_q5: What does a high volatility score represent?
quiz_q5_o1: The asset always goes up in value
quiz_q5_o2: The asset price moves significantly, both up and down
quiz_q5_o3: The asset is safer than average
quiz_q5_e: High volatility means large price movements in both directions — not just risk of decline, but also potential for sharp rises.
quiz_q6: What is a good example of a common beginner investment mistake?
quiz_q6_o1: Building an emergency fund before starting to invest
quiz_q6_o2: Consistent investing over time regardless of price (DCA)
quiz_q6_o3: Investing all savings in a single stock that received a "hot tip"
quiz_q6_e: Concentrating all savings in a single asset significantly increases specific risk — this is one of the most common mistakes made by beginning investors.
quiz_q7: What is the main difference between passive and active investing?
quiz_q7_o1: Passive tries to beat the market, active follows it
quiz_q7_o2: Active tries to beat the market, passive follows a low-cost index
quiz_q7_o3: There is no significant difference between them
quiz_q7_e: Active investing tries to select "better" assets than the market (usually at higher cost), while passive simply follows a broad index at low cost.

ai_insight_horizon_very_short: ⏳ Very short investment horizon. Over such a period, market volatility can have a significant impact on the outcome when the money may be needed.
ai_insight_horizon_medium_long: 📈 Medium-to-long horizon. Such a period allows compound returns and compound interest to become a significant factor in the outcome.

ai_insight_diversification_world: 🌎 The asset represents broader geographic diversification across markets. Such diversification may reduce dependence on a single market or geographic region.
ai_insight_diversification_sp500: 🇺🇸 The exposure is focused on large US companies. While there is variation between companies, there is still significant dependence on the performance of the US stock market.
ai_insight_diversification_nasdaq: 💻 The exposure is more focused on growth and technology companies. Such focus may increase growth potential, but also sensitivity to volatility and pricing changes.
ai_insight_diversification_bonds: 🛡️ Bonds tend to provide a more defensive character than a stock portfolio, but there are still risks such as interest rate changes, credit, and inflation.
ai_insight_diversification_cash: 💰 Cash provides high liquidity and low volatility, but over time there is exposure to inflation risk and the alternative cost of not investing the capital.
ai_insight_diversification_default: 🧩 The diversification level depends on the asset structure and additional assets in the portfolio. The system examines the asset as part of a broader picture, not as an isolated asset.
ai_insight_recommendation_very_short: ⚠️ In a very short horizon, significant weight should be given to liquidity and the ability to absorb a decline in value before the money is needed.
ai_insight_recommendation_short: ⚠️ In a relatively short horizon, it's important to examine whether the asset's volatility level is appropriate for when the money is expected to be needed.
ai_insight_recommendation_nasdaq: 📊 Due to the relative concentration in growth and technology companies, it's important to understand that the scenario may be more sensitive to market fluctuations. Diversification across assets can change the overall risk profile.
ai_insight_recommendation_sp500_long: 🚀 A long horizon can allow an investor to cope with volatility and take advantage of compound interest. However, actual returns are not guaranteed.
ai_insight_recommendation_world: 🌎 Broad geographic diversification can reduce dependence on a single region. However, this is still exposure to stock markets, so there is volatility.
ai_insight_recommendation_bonds: 🛡️ The bond character may be suitable for scenarios where relative stability is more important than maximizing growth potential, but bonds are not risk-free either.
ai_insight_recommendation_default: 🎯 It's advisable to examine the scenario in relation to the goal, investment horizon, and personal ability to cope with declines. The system presents an educational illustration and not a forecast of future returns.

quiz_q8: What is the main purpose of rebalancing a portfolio?
quiz_q8_o1: To sell everything when markets fall
quiz_q8_o3: To bring the allocation back to its target mix
quiz_q8_e: Rebalancing means periodically realigning the portfolio to its target allocation, which keeps risk at the intended level instead of drifting with market moves.
quiz_q9: Why does a low expense ratio matter over time?
quiz_q9_o1: Fees compound too, so small annual differences become large gaps
quiz_q9_e: An annual fee is charged every year on the whole balance, so even a 1% difference compounds into a very large gap over decades.
quiz_q10: What is a stock index like the S&P 500?
quiz_q10_o1: A basket that measures the performance of many companies together
quiz_q10_e: An index bundles many companies into one measure, letting investors follow the market as a whole instead of picking single stocks.
quiz_q11_o3: A rise in the general price level that erodes purchasing power
quiz_q11_e: Inflation means money buys less over time, which is why long-term savings need growth that at least keeps up with prices.
quiz_q12: What does liquidity mean for an investment?
quiz_q12_o3: How quickly and easily it can be converted to cash without a big loss
quiz_q12_e: Liquid assets can be sold quickly near their market price; illiquid assets may require time or a discount to sell.
quiz_q13: What usually happens to bond prices when interest rates rise?
quiz_q13_e: Existing bonds with lower fixed payments become less attractive when new bonds pay more, so their prices adjust downward.
quiz_q14: What is the relationship between risk and expected return?
quiz_q14_o1: Lower risk always means higher return
quiz_q14_o2: Higher expected return usually comes with higher risk
quiz_q14_e: Markets pay a premium for bearing uncertainty. A promise of high return with low risk is a classic warning sign.
quiz_q15: What is an emergency fund and why does it come before investing?
quiz_q15_o1: Cash covering several months of expenses so you never sell investments in a crisis
quiz_q15_o3: A fund that invests in emergencies
quiz_q15_e: An emergency fund prevents forced selling of investments at a bad time when unexpected expenses hit.
quiz_q16: What is the key difference between an ETF and a mutual fund?
quiz_q16_o2: ETFs trade on the exchange throughout the day like a stock
quiz_q16_e: Both pool investors' money, but ETFs trade continuously on the exchange while mutual fund units are priced once a day at NAV.
quiz_q17: Why can holding just one stock be risky even if the company is excellent?
quiz_q17_o1: It is illegal to hold one stock
quiz_q17_o2: Company-specific events can hit the whole investment at once
quiz_q17_e: Single-stock concentration exposes the whole portfolio to one company's specific risk, regardless of how good the company is.
quiz_q18: What does dollar-cost averaging (DCA) help with?
quiz_q18_o2: Reducing the impact of investing everything at a market peak
quiz_q18_e: Investing a fixed amount regularly buys more units when prices are low and fewer when high, smoothing the entry price over time.
quiz_q19_o1: The total debt of the company
quiz_q19_o2: Share price multiplied by the number of shares
quiz_q19_e: Market cap measures the equity-market size of a company, not its fair value or its profits.
quiz_q20: What does a high P/E ratio usually suggest?
quiz_q20_o2: Investors expect higher future growth, or the stock may be expensive
quiz_q20_e: A high P/E means investors pay more per unit of current earnings, usually reflecting growth expectations — or overpricing.
quiz_q21: What is the point of an investment horizon in planning?
quiz_q21_o3: It sets when you need the money, which shapes how much risk makes sense
quiz_q21_e: A long horizon allows riding out downturns; a short one calls for more stability because there is less time to recover.
quiz_q22_o3: A distribution of part of a company's profits to shareholders
quiz_q22_e: Dividends return part of the profit to owners, but they are never guaranteed and can be cut.
quiz_q23: What is NAV (net asset value) of a fund?
quiz_q23_o3: The fund's assets minus liabilities, divided by its units
quiz_q23_e: NAV is the per-unit value of what the fund actually holds; an ETF can trade slightly above or below it.
quiz_q24: Why does concentrating in one sector increase risk?
quiz_q24_o2: A shock to that sector hits the whole portfolio at once
quiz_q24_e: Sector shocks (regulation, demand shifts) hit all companies in the sector together, so concentration removes the protection of diversification.
quiz_q25: What is the main benefit of starting to invest early?
quiz_q25_o1: Markets only rise for young people
quiz_q25_o3: More time for compounding to work
quiz_q25_e: Compounding grows returns on returns, so each additional year multiplies the effect dramatically.

sim_page_subtitle: Build a simulated portfolio with virtual money, lock real entry prices for a fixed window, and learn allocation, rebalancing and risk by doing. Clearly simulated — no real money, no trading, no advice.

sim_builder_desc: Pick up to 6 assets and set their weights. Weights must total exactly 100%. Entry prices lock from real market data when you start.
sim_entry_locked_note: Positions and entry prices are locked for the whole window — no edits, no do-overs. Starting over means abandoning this run (abandoned runs never rank).
sim_error_nickname_too_long: Nickname can be at most 20 characters.
sim_error_nickname_private_info: Nickname can't contain contact details (email, links or phone numbers) — privacy first.
sim_error_weight_out_of_range: Each weight must be between 5% and 100%.
sim_error_duplicate_symbol: Each asset can appear only once.
sim_error_quote_unavailable: Real market data is unavailable for one of the assets — a simulation never starts on estimated prices.
sim_error_quote_simulated: A simulation can only start on real market data. Live quotes are unavailable right now — try again later.
sim_error_mixed_currencies: All assets must trade in the same currency for a fair comparison.
sim_prices_unavailable: Current prices are unavailable right now — nothing is estimated.
sim_complete_ready: The window has ended — finalize to record your result.
sim_abandon_confirm: Abandoning ends this run without ranking it. This cannot be undone. Continue?

learn_step_lesson_foundation: Start with risk, return, time horizon and diversification. Use Strategy Lab to compare approaches rather than memorize labels.
learn_step_lesson_builder: Connect allocation, fees and rebalancing. Compare strategies and explain what changes their outcomes.
learn_step_lesson_advanced: Interrogate assumptions, data freshness and failure modes. Compare strategy trade-offs without treating a model as a forecast.
learn_step_practice_text: Take a short quiz. Every answer includes an explanation, and your best score stays on this device.
learn_step_sim_text: Build a simulated portfolio on real entry quotes. Watch allocation and diversification without placing a trade or risking money.
learn_step_feedback_text: Ask the Copilot to challenge your assumptions, explain a missed concept or compare approaches. It teaches; it does not decide what to buy.
learn_feedback_before: Complete the diagnostic to get a learning sequence.
learn_feedback_lesson: Begin with the connected lesson. Aim to explain the trade-off in your own words before moving on.
learn_feedback_practice: You have a foundation. Now use retrieval practice to find what has actually stuck.
learn_feedback_simulation: Move from recall to application. In the simulation, write down why each allocation belongs before checking outcomes.
learn_feedback_reflection: You have practiced and applied. Ask the Copilot to challenge one assumption, then mark reflection complete only when you can state what changed.
learn_feedback_complete: Cycle complete. Review the weakest point, then start another cycle with a narrower question.
learn_feedback_quiz_review: Your latest short-quiz best score suggests a review will help. Revisit explanations for missed answers before simulation.
learn_feedback_sim_active: Your simulation is active. Avoid judging the decision only by short-term return; track allocation logic and what evidence would change your view.
learn_feedback_scope: This feedback uses activity stored on this device. It is rule-based learning guidance, not a claim that an AI model knows you or predicts markets.
learn_cycle_complete_text: Progress means you can explain the reasoning, not that every answer or simulation return was positive.
